lines.text: But the real way that actually this education happens is through networks and it's networks - that is part of the reason why when Linda was saying, "Well, what do you think about the Endeavor."
I said "It's really important."
He said, "When are you going to join?"
And I said, "Well, it's when not if."

glossary.ko: 할지 말지가 아니라 언제 하느냐의 문제다
glossary.easy: 반드시 일어날 일이고, 시기만 남았다는 뜻
glossary.nuance: 'It's a matter of when, not if'의 줄임. 확신을 강하게 드러내는 표현.
glossary.ex: Prices will go up. It's when, not if.
glossary.exKo: 가격은 오를 거야. 언제냐의 문제지, 오르냐 마냐의 문제가 아니야.

lines.text: It's because pulling networks of the shared information and the shared contacts, and the shared ability to find the right resources in order to create these massive institutions from nothing.
The education that you get from your network is actually, is what's critically important.

glossary.easy: 여러 사람이 가진 것을 한곳에 모으다
glossary.ex: We pooled our money to buy a gift.
glossary.tip: 자막엔 pulling이지만 의미상 pooling(공동으로 모으기)으로 이해하면 자연스럽다.

glossary.ex: She built her business from nothing.

glossary.easy: 없으면 안 될 정도로 아주 중요한
glossary.ex: Sleep is critically important for your health.

lines.text: For example, one of the things that I frequently tell entrepreneurs when an entrepreneur has an idea and they come to this I say, "Well, who should I talk to about it?"
It's like anyone who can possibly give you good feedback.

glossary.ex: I frequently travel for work.
glossary.exKo: 나는 일 때문에 자주 출장을 간다.

glossary.easy: 내 일이나 생각에 대한 다른 사람의 반응과 조언
glossary.ex: Thanks for the feedback on my presentation.

lines.text: Now, you'll publish it to the web maybe, because you don't necessarily get good feedback there.

But anyone who can give you good feedback, you go and tell them your idea and you talk to them about it, because the way that you have a competitive advantage is not because, "Well, I have this idea and other people don't have it, and the moment they have it I'm going to lose the competitive advantage."

glossary.ex: Expensive doesn't necessarily mean better.
glossary.exKo: 비싸다고 꼭 더 좋은 건 아니다.

glossary.easy: 다른 경쟁자보다 앞설 수 있는 강점
glossary.ex: Speed is our biggest competitive advantage.
glossary.exKo: 속도가 우리의 가장 큰 경쟁 우위다.

lines.text: It's because you're emotional in it.
You're assembling the network around your idea.

glossary.easy: 필요한 사람이나 부품을 모아서 하나로 만들다
glossary.ex: He's assembling a team for the new project.
glossary.exKo: 그는 새 프로젝트를 위해 팀을 꾸리고 있다.

lines.text: You're getting the co-founders, the employees, the potential customers.
You're moving and you're adjusting by talking to a number of people to get into the right target.

glossary.ex: The two co-founders met in college.
We kept testing until we got into the right target market.
glossary.exKo: 우리는 맞는 목표 시장을 찾을 때까지 계속 테스트했다.

lines.text: So, just someone else having the idea, that's not the impact; it's the network that essentially provides the education.

glossary.ex: The two plans are essentially the same.

lines.text: That's one of the reasons why I think that the Endeavor does, both in terms of its global network and in terms of events like this, are so critical for what entrepreneurial education really means.

glossary.ex: In terms of price, this phone is the best.
glossary.tip: 비즈니스 영어에서 매우 자주 쓴다. both in terms of A and in terms of B = A 면에서도 B 면에서도.

lines.text: It's of course extremely important because if you would look at it, I think the ability to have high impact product, services, and companies, I think that they're all global.
A global focus is, I think, extremely important.

glossary.ex: We want to focus on high-impact projects.
glossary.exKo: 우리는 영향력이 큰 프로젝트에 집중하고 싶다.

lines.text: Now, it's interesting when it gets to thinking about entrepreneurial companies and venture because part of the thing is that it has to start local and rooted.

glossary.easy: 특정 장소나 기반에 단단히 자리 잡은
glossary.ex: The company is deeply rooted in its hometown.
glossary.exKo: 그 회사는 고향에 깊이 뿌리내리고 있다.

lines.text: You have to get a team together, they have to have an idea, and they'd have to have an aperture that they're trying to drive the strategy through, you don't start with thinking about "how do I take over the whole globe with my new product, my new idea."

glossary.easy: 무엇에 집중할지 정한 좁은 시야나 범위
glossary.nuance: 원래는 카메라의 '조리개'. 비즈니스에서 '어디에 초점을 맞추는가'라는 비유로 쓴다.
glossary.ex: Narrow your aperture and focus on one market first.
glossary.exKo: 범위를 좁혀서 먼저 한 시장에 집중해라.
glossary.tip: 고급 비유 표현이라 듣고 이해만 할 수 있어도 충분하다.

glossary.easy: 어떤 곳을 전부 자기 것으로 만들다
glossary.ex: Smartphones have taken over our lives.

lines.text: You start thinking about it as, "How do I establish this as a strongly growing and ongoing concern that can fund its own expansion all the way to being a global entity, ultimately."

glossary.nuance: 보통 회계 용어 'going concern'(계속 기업). 여기서 concern은 '걱정'이 아니라 '회사, 사업체'.
glossary.ex: The bakery became a profitable, ongoing concern.
glossary.exKo: 그 빵집은 이익을 내며 계속 운영되는 사업체가 되었다.
glossary.tip: concern = 사업체(business)라는 뜻이 있다는 걸 기억하자.

glossary.ex: The company was able to fund its own expansion.
glossary.exKo: 그 회사는 스스로 확장 자금을 마련할 수 있었다.

lines.text: But all of the stuff starts locally; it starts with a region: Silicon Valley, Chile, Argentina, Jordan, local entrepreneurs and I can go through the whole list but then you don't want me doing that so I don't mean to leave anyone out.

glossary.ex: I don't want to leave anyone out of the invitation.
glossary.when: 명단을 말하다가 '혹시 빠진 분 있으면 죄송합니다'라고 할 때.

lines.text: Then how does that get onto the global stage?
That's one of the reasons I think putting time in this is extremely important.

glossary.easy: 전 세계 사람들이 보는 큰 무대
glossary.ex: K-pop is now on the global stage.
glossary.exKo: K-pop은 이제 세계 무대에 서 있다.

lines.text: But here's the thing I think is particularly interesting when it gets to entrepreneurial education, which is I think it's the importance of these means inthis learning is going beyond just founding companies.

Because if you look at it with the trends going on in terms of globalization, accelerating change in the markets, all of the institutions, not just the new companies building new products and services, have to adapt, which means, every individual now needs to act more entrepreneurial.
It doesn't mean that every individual is going to found a company.

glossary.ex: Technology is changing at an accelerating pace.
glossary.exKo: 기술은 점점 더 빠른 속도로 변하고 있다.

glossary.ex: You need to adapt to the new environment.

lines.text: Actually, I think, relatively few folks go through all of the different complexity in assembling all the different problems you needed to solve to found companies.

glossary.ex: She went through a lot last year.
Don't underestimate the complexity of the problem.

lines.text: But I think every career now is entrepreneurial, because I think it's both entrepreneurial by which the way that you operate within an organization, within a company is the market's changing and you need to help the company adapt, and then because the market is changing, what is a career path is no longer straight forward.

glossary.ex: He chose an unusual career path.
The instructions are pretty straightforward.
glossary.tip: 보통 한 단어 straightforward로 쓴다. 사람에게 쓰면 '솔직한'.

lines.text: It used to be like post-World War II; it's like, you joined a company, you're working with the ranks.
Then it got modified a little bit; whether you jump between companies, lost the work in the career ladder, I don't think there is any such thing as a career ladder anymore.

glossary.ex: She rose through the ranks to become CEO.
glossary.tip: rise through the ranks = 밑바닥에서부터 승진하다.

glossary.easy: 한 회사 안에서 한 단계씩 올라가는 승진 구조
glossary.ex: He climbed the career ladder quickly.

lines.text: I think that the pattern by which you develop a skill set and a set of work, a set of ability, a network, skills and the rest, I think actually much more mirrors how entrepreneurs live and work than anything else.

glossary.easy: 한 사람이 가진 여러 능력과 기술의 묶음
glossary.ex: Her skill set is perfect for this job.
glossary.exKo: 그녀의 역량은 이 일에 딱 맞는다.

glossary.ex: The movie mirrors real life.
glossary.exKo: 그 영화는 실제 삶을 그대로 닮았다.

lines.text: I think that's part of the reason of what we're doing is important, because I think it has that kind of global impact.
